main_point.en: When we’re devoted to following Jesus, we will live in obedience to God’s Word.
main_point.zh-Hant: 當我們專心跟隨耶穌時，我們就會活在順服神話語的生命中。

christ_connection.en: Jesus completely obeyed God and identified with sinful humans by being baptized. His baptism points to His death on the cross and to His resurrection from the grave. For those of us in Christ, the words spoken over Jesus at His baptism are also true of us: We are the Father’s beloved children with whom He is pleased.
christ_connection.zh-Hant: 耶穌完全順服神，並藉著受洗與有罪的人類認同。祂的洗禮指向祂在十字架上的死，也指向祂從墳墓裡的復活。對於我們這些在基督裡的人來說，在耶穌受洗時所說的話，同樣適用於我們：我們是天父所愛的兒女，是祂所喜悅的。

title.zh-Hant: 耶穌的順服彰顯了祂的身分

content.en:
13 Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan to John, to be baptized by him. 
14 John would have prevented him, saying, “I need to be baptized by you, and do you come to me?” 
15 But Jesus answered him, “Let it be so now, for thus it is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness.” Then he consented. 
16 And when Jesus was baptized, immediately he went up from the water, and behold, the heavens were opened to him, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and coming to rest on him; 
17 and behold, a voice from heaven said, “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.”
content.zh-Hant:
13 當下，耶穌從加利利來到約旦河，見了約翰，要受他的洗。
14 約翰想要攔住他，說：「我當受你的洗，你反倒上我這裏來嗎？」
15 耶穌回答說：「你暫且許我，因為我們理當這樣盡諸般的義。」於是約翰許了他。
16 耶穌受了洗，隨即從水裏上來。天忽然為他開了，他就看見神的靈彷彿鴿子降下，落在他身上。
17 從天上有聲音說：「這是我的愛子，我所喜悅的。」

title.zh-Hant: 我們的順服彰顯我們的身分

content.en:
29 The next day he saw Jesus coming toward him, and said, “Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world! 
30 This is he of whom I said, ‘After me comes a man who ranks before me, because he was before me.’ 
31 I myself did not know him, but for this purpose I came baptizing with water, that he might be revealed to Israel.” 
32 And John bore witness: “I saw the Spirit descend from heaven like a dove, and it remained on him. 
33 I myself did not know him, but he who sent me to baptize with water said to me, ‘He on whom you see the Spirit descend and remain, this is he who baptizes with the Holy Spirit.’ 
34 And I have seen and have borne witness that this is the Son of God.”
content.zh-Hant:
29 次日，約翰看見耶穌來到他那裏，就說：「看哪，神的羔羊，除去世人罪孽的！
30 這就是我曾說：『有一位在我以後來、反成了在我以前的，因他本來在我以前。』
31 我先前不認識他，如今我來用水施洗，為要叫他顯明給以色列人。」
32 約翰又作見證說：「我曾看見聖靈，彷彿鴿子從天降下，住在他的身上。
33 我先前不認識他，只是那差我來用水施洗的、對我說：『你看見聖靈降下來，住在誰的身上，誰就是用聖靈施洗的。』
34 我看見了，就證明這是神的兒子。」

content.en: Leaders: Your life reveals who or what you’re devoted to; may the sum of it point to Jesus only.
content.zh-Hant: 帶領者：你的生命彰顯出你所委身、所投入的對象是誰或是甚麼；願這一切的總和唯獨指向耶穌。

title.zh-Hant: 耶穌的順服彰顯了祂的身分

content.en: “Jesus’s baptism was unique. It was not a ‘baptism of repentance’ (as John’s was) nor was it a ‘Christian baptism’ (as ours is today). But it was an identifying step of obedience at the beginning of Jesus’s public ministry. Jesus would not have been fully obedient if he had bypassed this step that seemed to John to be unnecessary for the Holy One (3:14).”⁶
content.zh-Hant: 「耶穌的洗禮是獨一無二的。它既不是（約翰所施的那種）『悔改的洗禮』，也不是（今天我們所受的那種）『基督徒的洗禮』。相反地，它是耶穌在公開事奉之初一個表明身分的順服舉動。若耶穌略過了這一步——這一步在約翰看來對這位聖者是不必要的（3:14）——祂就不算是完全順服了。」⁶

content.en: “Jesus’s baptism is an identification with sinners. Jesus came, according to Isaiah 53:12, to be ‘counted among the rebels,’ and ultimately this has to do with their sin, though Jesus Himself had no sin (Heb. 4:15). We identify with Jesus when we are baptized, being united to Him in His life, death, and resurrection, so it makes sense that baptism is in a very real sense His identification with us. He who had no sin took His place among those who had no righteousness. This is the essence of what Jesus came to do (2 Cor. 5:21). . . . Jesus also sets an example for us. His baptism is an example for saints. Jesus models obedience for His followers by being baptized, which is an obedience that He will eventually command His followers to submit to (Matt. 28:20). . . . It is also a picture of salvation. Baptism pictures death and resurrection to new life, such that here at the beginning of Jesus’s ministry, we get a picture of the climax of this ministry. That is, His immersion portrays His future death and resurrection. And now, every person who trusts in Christ for salvation is baptized, immersed in water, as a picture of our dying to sin and to ourselves and rising to new life in Christ.”⁷
content.zh-Hant: 「耶穌的洗禮是與罪人的認同。根據以賽亞書 53:12，耶穌來是要『被列在罪犯之中』，這歸根究柢與他們的罪有關，儘管耶穌自己並無罪（希伯來書 4:15）。當我們受洗時，我們與耶穌認同，在祂的生、死、復活裏與祂聯合，所以在一個非常真實的意義上，洗禮乃是祂與我們的認同，這是說得通的。那無罪的一位，與那些毫無義的人站在同一處。這正是耶穌前來要成就之事的精髓（哥林多後書 5:21）。……耶穌也為我們立下榜樣。祂的洗禮是給聖徒的榜樣。耶穌藉著受洗為祂的跟隨者示範順服，這順服是祂最終要吩咐祂的跟隨者去遵行的（馬太福音 28:20）。……它也是救恩的一幅圖畫。洗禮描繪出死亡與復活進入新生命，以致在耶穌事奉的起初，我們就得見這事奉高峰的一幅圖畫。也就是說，祂的浸入水中描繪出祂將來的死與復活。如今，每一位信靠基督得救的人都受洗、被浸入水中，作為我們向罪、向自己死去，並在基督裏復活進入新生命的一幅圖畫。」⁷

title.zh-Hant: 我們的順服彰顯我們的身分

content.en: “In Revelation 5 we briefly glimpse the worship of Jesus in heaven, and we hear that the ‘Lion from the tribe of Judah . . . has conquered’ (v. 5). But then our eyes look up and we see not a Lion but a Lamb, standing yet looking as if he had been slaughtered. Bowing all around him are people singing, ‘Worthy is the Lamb who was slaughtered’ (v. 12). Jesus conquered sin, death, and hell by sacrificing himself as our substitute. He was a Lamb offered by God for our sin.”⁸
content.zh-Hant: 「在啟示錄第 5 章，我們短暫地一窺天上對耶穌的敬拜，我們聽見那『猶大支派中的獅子……已經得勝』（第 5 節）。但接著我們舉目觀看，看見的卻不是一頭獅子，而是一隻羔羊，站立著，卻像是被殺過的。環繞在祂四圍下拜的眾人唱著：『曾被殺的羔羊是配得的』（第 12 節）。耶穌藉著獻上自己作我們的替代，勝過了罪、死亡和陰間。祂是神為我們的罪所獻上的羔羊。」⁸

content.en: Baptism existed before the New Testament. Jewish people had taken part in ceremonial water cleansing for a long time to honor God’s commands concerning purity. Sometime during the second century BC (Second Temple period), Jews developed a stepped bath, called a “mikveh.” Archaeologists discovered mikvehs in private homes and in public spaces, like the pools of Siloam and Bathesda, to accommodate large crowds. These pools often attracted the sick, the “unclean” or “blemished,” providing a backdrop for some of Jesus’s healings. Before entering the temple, praying, or other sacred acts, Jews washed themselves in mikvehs, symbolically representing repentance and purification. When John the Baptist called everyone to repent and be baptized, he did so within this context. But Jesus’s baptism sent a different message: The Son of God would cleanse us of sin once and for all and baptize us in a new way, through the Holy Spirit. His sacrifice altered water cleansing forever; rather than continually taking part in it to be ritually clean, we are baptized once, as a symbol of Jesus’s blood continually purifying us, making us clean for good, and as a declaration of obedience to the Father.
content.zh-Hant: 洗禮在新約之前就已存在。長久以來，猶太人一直參與禮儀性的潔淨水禮，以尊崇神有關潔淨的誡命。大約在主前二世紀（第二聖殿時期），猶太人發展出一種帶階梯的浸洗池，稱為「米克瓦（mikveh）」。考古學家在私人住宅和公共場所都發現了米克瓦，例如西羅亞池和畢士大池，用以容納大批人群。這些池子常吸引病患、「不潔」或「有殘疾」的人，成為耶穌某些醫治神蹟的背景。在進入聖殿、禱告或進行其他神聖行為之前，猶太人會在米克瓦中潔淨自己，象徵性地代表悔改與潔淨。當施洗約翰呼召眾人悔改受洗時，他正是在這樣的背景下如此行的。但耶穌的洗禮傳遞了一個不同的信息：神的兒子將要一次而永遠地潔淨我們的罪，並以一種嶄新的方式，藉著聖靈為我們施洗。祂的犧牲永遠改變了潔淨水禮；我們不再需要不斷地參與其中以求禮儀上的潔淨，而是一次受洗，作為耶穌寶血不斷潔淨我們、使我們永遠潔淨的象徵，也作為向父順服的宣告。

content.en: Christian baptism is the immersion of a believer in water in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. It is an act of obedience symbolizing the believer’s faith in a crucified, buried, and risen Savior, the believer’s death to sin, the burial of the old life, and the resurrection to walk in newness of life in Christ Jesus. It is a testimony of faith in the final resurrection of the dead. Baptism is a church ordinance and comes before the privileges of church membership and taking part in the Lord’s Supper.
content.zh-Hant: 基督徒的洗禮，是奉父、子、聖靈的名將信徒浸入水中。這是一個順服的行動，象徵著信徒對那位被釘十字架、被埋葬、又復活之救主的信心，象徵著信徒向罪而死、舊生命的埋葬，以及復活過來、在基督耶穌裡以新生的樣式行事為人。它也是對將來死人復活的信心見證。洗禮是教會的禮儀，先於作教會成員的權利，也先於領受聖餐的權利。

content.en: God, thank you for sending your son, who obediently identified with us in every way to redeem us from sin. We choose to live in obedience to your word, as an outward expression of our commitment and devotion to you.
content.zh-Hant: 神啊，感謝祢差遣祢的兒子，祂順服地在各方面與我們認同，好將我們從罪中救贖出來。我們選擇活出對祢話語的順服，作為我們對祢委身與投入的外在表達。

question.en: Let’s check in on how you’re doing spiritually. Last week, we learned that worldly living shouldn’t be “normal” for believers, who are called to live as citizens of heaven. How have you made efforts to look at things with this perspective? What area of your life is a struggle when it comes to this mindset?
question.zh-Hant: 讓我們一同檢視你近來的屬靈光景。上週，我們學到屬世的生活方式不應成為信徒的「常態」，因為信徒蒙召要活出天上國民的樣式。你曾如何努力以這樣的視角來看待各樣的事？在這種心態上，你生命中的哪個領域是你所掙扎的？

instructions.en:
These optional activities are designed to help your students interact. You’ll find a Discussion Activity and a Cultural Connection, which touches on a relevant topic in today’s teen culture. Each group is different, so adapt these activities to fit your group’s needs. The goal is for students to connect more to the lesson as they connect to the topic and to one another.

Ask the following questions, allowing time for students to share responses:
instructions.zh-Hant:
這些選擇性的活動旨在幫助你的學生彼此互動。你會看到一個討論活動和一個文化連結，後者觸及當今青少年文化中一個相關的主題。每個小組都不一樣，所以請調整這些活動以配合你小組的需要。目標是讓學生在與主題和彼此連結的同時，也能更深地與課程連結。

提出以下問題，讓學生有時間分享他們的回應：

question.en: When have you felt like a certain rule didn’t apply to you?
question.zh-Hant: 你甚麼時候曾覺得某條規矩不適用在你身上？

question.en: How do you respond in those times? Do you obey or rebel?
question.zh-Hant: 在那些時候你如何回應？你是順從還是反叛？

question.en: Can you think of a time when your whole class, group, or team was punished because of only one person’s actions? Was that fair? Explain.
question.zh-Hant: 你能想到有一次，你的全班、整組或整隊因為只有一個人的行為而受罰嗎？那公平嗎？請說明。

content.en: Sometimes we get in a situation where a rule may not apply to us, but we’re expected to follow it anyway. Though Jesus is fully God, He was fully man. He lived in perfect obedience, and today, we’ll learn that He was baptized, not because He had sinned and needed to repent but because He was our model for obeying the Father and identified Himself with us to save us.
content.zh-Hant: 有時我們會遇到某條規矩似乎不適用於我們，但我們卻仍被期待要去遵守。耶穌雖然是完全的神，祂也是完全的人。祂活出了完全的順服；今天我們要學到，祂受洗並非因為祂犯了罪、需要悔改，而是因為祂是我們順服父的榜樣，並且與我們認同以拯救我們。

cultural_connection.en: What’s the big deal with baptism? Can we skip that step? First, baptism doesn’t save us from sin or make us clean. When we confess Jesus as Lord (confessing and turning from sin) and believe He was raised from death, we are saved (Rom. 10:9). But Jesus commanded us to follow His example in baptism (Matt. 28:18-20). Jesus, who had not sinned, was baptized to show us the way of obedience. Baptism is a declaration of our salvation: Our old self is buried and we’re new creations, able to walk in a totally new way because of the Holy Spirit (Rom. 6:3-5). Many times, people resist baptism because they’re fearful of being in front of others or because they don’t feel it’s necessary. But Jesus commanded it, so we’re called to obey. We must ask ourselves how we can inwardly commit our heart yet outwardly refuse to obey Him in this matter—in any matter. Jesus didn’t command us to do anything that He didn’t do too. He showed us how. We can obediently follow Him and trust His example.
cultural_connection.zh-Hant: 洗禮有甚麼大不了的？我們可以跳過那一步嗎？首先，洗禮並不能救我們脫離罪，也不能使我們潔淨。當我們認耶穌為主（承認並轉離罪），並相信祂已從死裡復活，我們就得救了（羅 10:9）。但耶穌命令我們要效法祂的榜樣去受洗（太 28:18-20）。耶穌本沒有犯罪，卻受了洗，為要向我們顯明順服的道路。洗禮是我們得救的宣告：我們的舊我已被埋葬，我們是新造的人，因著聖靈能以一種全新的方式而行（羅 6:3-5）。很多時候，人們抗拒受洗，是因為害怕站在眾人面前，或是因為覺得沒有必要。但耶穌既已命令，我們就蒙召去順服。我們必須自問：怎能一面內心委身，一面卻在這件事上——或在任何事上——外在地拒絕順服祂呢？耶穌從未命令我們去做任何祂自己沒有做過的事。祂已向我們示範了怎樣做。我們可以順服地跟隨祂，並信靠祂的榜樣。

title.zh-Hant: 耶穌的順服彰顯了祂的身分

question.en: How important is fairness to you? How have you seen life be unfair?
question.zh-Hant: 公平對你有多重要？你曾見過生命中哪些不公平的事？

answer.en: Most of us value fairness. Even small children recognize unfair situations. But some of us see unfairness only when it applies to ourselves. We cry out for justice only when we’re treated unjustly. The difficult truth is that what’s actually “fair” for all of us is punishment. Why? Because the punishment for sin is death, and we’ve all sinned. What’s fair is for all of us to pay the debt we owe. But Jesus stepped in our place to suffer and die—unfairly. So, is life fair? Not at all, and praise God! Because of Jesus, we don’t get what’s fair or what we deserve; we get forgiveness and life.
answer.zh-Hant: 我們大多數人都看重公平。連小孩子都能辨認出不公平的情況。但我們當中有些人只有在事情臨到自己身上時才看見不公平。我們只有在自己受到不公正對待時才呼求公義。難以接受的真相是：對我們所有人而言，真正「公平」的其實是刑罰。為甚麼？因為罪的刑罰就是死，而我們都犯了罪。公平的做法是我們所有人都償還我們所欠的債。但耶穌卻站到我們的位置上受苦、受死——這是不公平的。那麼，生命公平嗎？一點也不，但要讚美神！因著耶穌，我們得著的不是公平、不是我們所應得的；我們得著的是赦免與生命。

question.en: Jesus was sinless, so why did He insist on being baptized?
question.zh-Hant: 耶穌是無罪的，那祂為甚麼堅持要受洗？

answer.en: Leaders: Share context on mikveh to help students understand John’s confusion and the context of these baptisms. John was understandably confused about Jesus asking for baptism. The purpose of mikveh was repentance and symbolic cleansing, but Jesus was sinless. By taking part in baptism, Jesus transformed its meaning! Baptism was His outward declaration of obedience to the Father—of already being clean and already belonging to God. To redeem us, Jesus identified with us. He began His ministry with this act of obedience—an act He later commanded for all believers, displaying the same outward declaration of being clean and belonging to God.
answer.zh-Hant: 帶領者：分享有關米克瓦的背景，幫助學生理解約翰的困惑以及這些洗禮的背景。約翰對耶穌要求受洗感到困惑是可以理解的。米克瓦的目的是悔改與象徵性的潔淨，但耶穌是無罪的。藉著參與洗禮，耶穌改變了它的意義！洗禮是祂向父順服的外在宣告——宣告祂本已潔淨、本已屬於神。為了救贖我們，耶穌與我們認同。祂以這個順服的舉動開始了祂的事奉——這舉動是祂後來吩咐所有信徒去遵行的，同樣彰顯出潔淨與屬於神的外在宣告。

question.en: When have you needed someone to back you up or support you? Why was it important that God confirmed Jesus’s identity at His baptism?
question.zh-Hant: 你甚麼時候曾需要有人支持你、為你撐腰？為甚麼神在耶穌受洗時確認祂的身分是重要的？

answer.en: Confirmation provides proof and assurance. For example, if you want people to believe you’re telling the truth, having others confirm your story makes it more believable. Jesus’s baptism was monumental for several reasons. Jesus, a seemingly unimportant man from the small town of Galilee, was beginning His public ministry. But we know now what many people didn’t know then: Jesus was so much more than a good teacher from Galilee. Jesus is the eternal Son of God. At the start of Jesus’s ministry, God opened the heavens and verbally affirmed Jesus’s obedience, expressing pride for His Son and echoing prophecy (Isa. 42:1). Every Person of the Trinity was present: God the Father observed God the Son’s obedience, while God the Holy Spirit rested on the Son like a dove! We get a beautiful glimpse of the Father’s loving relationship with His Son as He applauded Jesus’s obedience—and not just obedience in this moment but for Jesus’s entire life leading up to this moment. At Jesus’s baptism, God confirmed His Son’s identity as if saying, “This is my Son, the chosen One; He is who He claims to be! And He makes me proud.”
answer.zh-Hant: 確認提供了證明與保證。舉例來說，如果你想要人相信你說的是實話，有其他人證實你的說法會使它更可信。耶穌的洗禮之所以意義重大，有幾個原因。耶穌，一位看似無足輕重、來自加利利小鎮的人，正要開始祂的公開事奉。但我們如今知道許多當時的人所不知道的事：耶穌遠不只是一位來自加利利的好教師。耶穌是神永恆的兒子。在耶穌事奉的起初，神開了天，親口肯定了耶穌的順服，為祂的兒子表達喜悅，並呼應了預言（以賽亞書 42:1）。三位一體的每一個位格都在場：父神觀看子神的順服，而聖靈神則如鴿子降下，落在子的身上！當父為耶穌的順服喝采時，我們得以美好地一窺父與子之間充滿慈愛的關係——這不僅是此刻的順服，更是耶穌直到這一刻為止一生的順服。在耶穌受洗時，神確認了祂兒子的身分，彷彿在說：「這是我的兒子，是那蒙揀選的一位；祂正是祂所宣稱的那一位！祂使我引以為榮。」

title.zh-Hant: 我們的順服彰顯我們的身分

question.en: What causes us to act pridefully or arrogantly? How do you keep this in check?
question.zh-Hant: 是甚麼使我們行事驕傲或自大？你如何約束這種傾向？

answer.en: John was Jesus’s cousin. People were drawn to him out of curiosity about his bold message and his lifestyle. John could’ve hoarded the praise and attention and leaned into arrogance. The reality is that sometimes we do really great things. We have really great ideas, talents, and achievements. Keeping our pride in check isn’t easy. We need the Holy Spirit to convict us of pride and remind us of who we are without Jesus. Without His help, we drift into glorifying ourselves and believing we’re self-sufficient, but anything good in us comes from the Lord (James 1:17). If God gives you a platform or any type of success, point all praise and curiosity and attention back to Jesus. He is the greater One, worthy of all praise.
answer.zh-Hant: 約翰是耶穌的表兄。人們因著好奇他大膽的信息和他的生活方式而被吸引到他那裏。約翰大可獨佔這些讚美與關注，並任由自己陷入狂妄。事實是，有時候我們確實做了一些很了不起的事。我們有很棒的點子、才幹和成就。要約束我們的驕傲並不容易。我們需要聖靈使我們為驕傲知罪自責，並提醒我們：沒有耶穌，我們算不得甚麼。若沒有祂的幫助，我們就會飄向榮耀自己、以為自己自給自足；但我們裏面一切美善的都是從主而來的（雅各書 1:17）。如果神給你一個舞台或任何形式的成功，就把一切讚美、好奇與關注都導回到耶穌身上。祂是那更大的一位，配得一切讚美。

question.en: How do we know what John believed about Jesus? How will people know what we believe?
question.zh-Hant: 我們怎麼知道約翰對耶穌的信念是甚麼？別人又將如何知道我們所相信的是甚麼？

answer.en: John boldly stated who he knew Jesus to be—the Son of God, not simply a good teacher or role model. He didn’t soften his words or speak vaguely so that everyone would agree with him. John knew Jesus was the Lamb, who would do what thousands on thousands of sacrificial lambs never did: heal our sin and offer permanent forgiveness. John’s words testified about Jesus, but his actions confirmed his beliefs. He pointed to Jesus as the greater One. Our words and actions reveal if we belong to Jesus. If we claim to follow Him, then we can’t be neutral concerning His identity; we can’t speak vaguely; we can’t believe from a safe distance.
answer.zh-Hant: 約翰大膽地宣告他所認識的耶穌是誰——是神的兒子，而不只是一位好教師或榜樣。他沒有為了讓人人都認同他而軟化他的話語或含糊其辭。約翰知道耶穌就是那羔羊，祂要成就那千千萬萬隻獻祭的羔羊從未成就的事：醫治我們的罪，並賜下永久的赦免。約翰的話語為耶穌作見證，但他的行為證實了他的信念。他指向耶穌是那更大的一位。我們的言語和行為顯明我們是否屬於耶穌。如果我們宣稱跟隨祂，那麼我們就不能對祂的身分保持中立；我們不能含糊其辭；我們不能從安全的距離之外去相信。

question.en: What does it mean to be devoted? What are things people can tell you’re devoted to right now?
question.zh-Hant: 「專心委身」是甚麼意思？現在有哪些事情能讓別人看出你所專心委身的對象？

answer.en: We’re all devoted to something or to someone, and people can tell what it is. How? The object of our devotion becomes clear in the way we talk, how we act, the places we go or don’t go, and how we spend our time. Can people tell that your heart is devoted to Jesus above all else? Would people say that you’re more devoted to school, sports, music, money, clothes, popularity, friends, a boyfriend or girlfriend? Here’s the truth: So many of these things aren’t bad or sinful, but they become idols if we’re devoted to them instead of God. When we’re wholly devoted to God, He uses the things we love and our talents as instruments to reach others! Our devotion to God opens the door for everything else to have greater purpose.
answer.zh-Hant: 我們每個人都委身投入於某件事或某個人，而人們能看出那是甚麼。怎麼看出來？我們所委身投入的對象，會在我們說話的方式、行事的態度、我們去或不去的地方，以及我們如何運用時間上顯明出來。人們能看出你的心是高過一切地委身於耶穌嗎？人們會說你更委身於學業、運動、音樂、金錢、衣著、名氣、朋友、男朋友或女朋友嗎？真相是這樣的：這許多事物本身並不壞、也不是罪，但如果我們委身於它們而非神，它們就成了偶像。當我們全心委身於神時，祂就使用我們所愛的事物和我們的才幹，作為觸及他人的器皿！我們對神的委身，為其他一切事物開了門，使它們能有更大的目的。

question.en: How could your lifestyle confuse people about your belief in Jesus? Why does your obedience to God matter?
question.zh-Hant: 你的生活方式可能如何使別人對你信耶穌一事感到困惑？為甚麼你對神的順服很重要？

answer.en: If our lifestyle causes confusion about Jesus, then we must examine why. People won’t believe our message if our lifestyle contradicts it; they won’t believe Jesus can change them if we don’t live changed. Like John, we must clearly vocalize who Jesus is but without being unloving or rude; we don’t reflect Jesus when we berate people while sharing our beliefs. But God calls us to bold faith, and this includes speaking out when He leads us to do so. We can make our belief in Jesus clear by loving people, in how we talk to and about others, by making godly choices instead of sinful ones. Jesus walked in perfect obedience and showed us how to live. While we won’t be perfect, we can follow Jesus’s lead and obey God’s Word, even when others disagree. Our lifestyle must point people to Jesus, not away from Him. If the way we live confuses people, then we must determine where we’re disobeying God’s Word. Our obedience displays the power of the gospel to a lost world and gives people hope that God can save and change them too.
answer.zh-Hant: 如果我們的生活方式使人對耶穌感到困惑，那麼我們就必須省察其中的原因。如果我們的生活方式與我們的信息相矛盾，人們就不會相信我們的信息；如果我們沒有活出改變的樣式，人們就不會相信耶穌能改變他們。像約翰一樣，我們必須清楚地說出耶穌是誰，卻不能沒有愛心或粗魯無禮；當我們在分享信念時苛責他人，我們就沒有反映出耶穌。但神呼召我們要有大膽的信心，這包括在祂帶領我們發聲時勇於出聲。我們可以藉著愛人、藉著我們與人交談及談論他人的方式、藉著做出敬虔而非罪惡的選擇，來使我們對耶穌的信念清晰可見。耶穌行在完全的順服中，並向我們示範了該如何生活。雖然我們不會做到完全，但我們可以跟隨耶穌的帶領，順服神的話語，即使他人不認同也是如此。我們的生活方式必須將人指向耶穌，而非使人遠離祂。如果我們生活的方式使人困惑，那麼我們就必須查明我們在哪裏違背了神的話語。我們的順服向一個失喪的世界彰顯出福音的大能，並給人盼望：神也能拯救並改變他們。

content.en:
People wear jerseys to show they are fans of an athlete, specific colors to show support for a school or team, and rings if they get married—all examples of ways that people can publicly display their loyalty to someone or something. For example, if you decided to wear someone else’s wedding ring for the day, would that make you married? No way! What makes someone married is not the jewelry they wear but the covenant love two people enter into before God and others. A wedding ring, as precious as it might be, is still just a symbol for the commitment made. Baptism works in a similar way. It is a powerful act of obedience that tells the world who you are loyal to, but it is still a symbol to show the work that Jesus has already done in your life.

When Peter said that baptism “now saves you,” he did not say that the act of being submerged into water automatically made you a Christian, but he explained that baptism is a symbol that shows others you have been saved by placing your faith in Jesus. To be very clear: We are forgiven of all sin and saved only when we repent, believe, and surrender our lives to Jesus, who died on the cross and rose from the dead to reign victoriously as King forever. This gift of salvation was always meant to be shared with others as an act of obedience. We obey God when we not only commit to follow Him for the rest of our days but also when we share with others that we have been made new by God and are now loyal to Him alone. If you have called on Jesus for salvation but have not been baptized, talk to a trusted adult today about this step of obedience!
content.zh-Hant:
人們穿球衣來表明自己是某位運動員的球迷，穿特定的顏色來表達對某所學校或某支球隊的支持，結婚時戴上戒指——這些都是人們公開展示自己對某人或某事忠誠的方式。舉例來說，如果你決定戴上別人的結婚戒指一整天，這會使你成為已婚的人嗎？當然不會！使一個人成為已婚者的，不是他們所戴的首飾，而是兩個人在神與眾人面前所立的盟約之愛。一枚結婚戒指，無論多麼珍貴，仍然只是所立承諾的一個象徵。洗禮的運作方式與此類似。它是一個大有能力的順服行動，向世界宣告你效忠於誰，但它仍然只是一個象徵，彰顯耶穌已經在你生命中所成就的工作。

當彼得說洗禮「現在……也拯救你們」時，他並不是說被浸入水中這個行動會自動使你成為基督徒，而是解釋洗禮乃是一個象徵，向別人顯明你已經藉著把信心放在耶穌身上而得救。要說得非常清楚：唯有當我們悔改、相信，並將生命交託給耶穌時，我們一切的罪才得赦免、才得拯救——這位耶穌在十字架上受死，又從死裡復活，永遠作王得勝掌權。這救恩的禮物，向來就是要作為一個順服的行動與他人分享的。當我們不僅委身餘生跟隨神，也向別人分享我們已被神更新、如今單單效忠於祂時，我們就是在順服神。如果你已經呼求耶穌得著救恩，卻還沒有受洗，今天就去找一位你信任的成年人談談這一步順服吧！

question.en: In your own words, what is baptism? Why is it important?
question.zh-Hant: 用你自己的話說，洗禮是甚麼？為甚麼它很重要？

question.en: If you have already been baptized, write out a prayer reflecting on that day and thanking God for saving you. If you haven’t been baptized, write out a prayer asking God for courage to talk to someone about taking this next step.
question.zh-Hant: 如果你已經受過洗，寫下一個禱告，回想那一天，並為神拯救了你而感謝祂。如果你還沒有受洗，寫下一個禱告，求神賜你勇氣去找人談談踏出這下一步。

prayer.en: God, thank you for saving me by the death and resurrection of Jesus. Give me the courage to choose obedience. You are always worth following and sharing!
prayer.zh-Hant: 神啊，感謝祢藉著耶穌的死與復活拯救了我。求祢賜我勇氣選擇順服。祢永遠值得跟隨、值得傳揚！

content.en:
Every time we watch someone get baptized, we watch the gospel demonstrated. If we aren’t careful, we can get so used to watching baptisms that we treat them as normal and miss the beauty, hope, and power each baptism declares. Someone going under the water symbolizes death—Jesus’s death and ours. Salvation is only possible because Jesus first laid down His life for us on the cross. We also died to sin and our old ways of living when we surrendered our lives to Jesus. Then, someone coming out of the water symbolizes life—abundant life now and eternal life forever, all because of Jesus.

Because of God’s great love and mercy, death is never the end of the story for anyone who loves God and truly walks with Him. Baptism reminds us of an important truth: Resurrection and new life come only after death. Abundant and eternal life are only made possible by Jesus first dying on the cross. New life is only made possible by us first dying to our old self and our sin. God’s Word promises that because of Jesus, sin and death have been defeated. When we surrender to Jesus, we put to death our old ways and are made alive in Christ permanently. Praise God! Here’s the thing—when we follow Jesus, sin no longer has power over our lives because Jesus defeated sin and death, but for the rest of our days on earth, sin still has presence in our lives. We are no longer slaves to sin, which is great news. But, we still need to practice daily repentance and self-control, considering ourselves dead to sin and instead alive to God.
content.zh-Hant:
每一次我們看著有人受洗，我們都是在觀看福音被演示出來。如果我們不小心，就會太習慣觀看洗禮，以致把它們當作平常事，而錯過了每一次洗禮所宣告的美麗、盼望與能力。有人被浸入水中，象徵著死——耶穌的死，也是我們的死。救恩之所以可能，唯獨因為耶穌首先在十字架上為我們捨了自己的生命。當我們把生命交託給耶穌時，我們也向罪、向自己舊有的生活方式死了。然後，有人從水裡上來，象徵著生命——如今豐盛的生命，以及永遠的永生，這一切都是因著耶穌。

因著神偉大的慈愛與憐憫，對任何愛神並真正與祂同行的人來說，死絕不是故事的結局。洗禮提醒我們一個重要的真理：復活與新生命唯有在死之後才會臨到。豐盛而永恆的生命，唯有藉著耶穌首先在十字架上受死才成為可能。新生命也唯有藉著我們首先向舊我與罪死了才成為可能。神的話語應許：因著耶穌，罪與死已被擊敗。當我們降服於耶穌時，我們就治死了自己舊有的方式，並永遠地在基督裡活過來。讚美神！重點是這樣——當我們跟隨耶穌時，罪不再在我們生命中掌權，因為耶穌已經擊敗了罪與死；但在我們地上餘下的日子裡，罪仍然存在於我們的生命中。我們不再作罪的奴僕，這是天大的好消息。但是，我們仍然需要天天操練悔改與自制，看自己是向罪死了，反倒向神活著。

question.en: How are you personally encouraged by the truth that sin no longer has power in your life because of Jesus?
question.zh-Hant: 罪不再在你生命中掌權——這個真理是因著耶穌而成的。你個人如何從中得著鼓勵？

question.en: Write out a prayer to God thanking him for defeating death and sin on your behalf and for calling you to abundant life now and in eternity.
question.zh-Hant: 寫下一個禱告給神，感謝祂為你擊敗了死亡與罪，並呼召你進入如今與永恆中的豐盛生命。

prayer.en: God, may watching someone get baptized never get old because of its picture of the gospel. Thank you for declaring me freed from the power of sin. Help me to repent and run back to you.
prayer.zh-Hant: 神啊，願觀看有人受洗這事，永不因它所描繪的福音圖畫而變得陳舊。感謝祢宣告我已從罪的權勢中得釋放。求祢幫助我悔改，並奔回到祢那裡。

content.en:
Earlier this week, we studied Matthew’s and John’s accounts of Jesus’s baptism, when God declared that Jesus was His beloved Son. Today’s passage shows us that through Jesus, we are also declared God’s dearly-loved children! The fact that we get to be called children of God is further proof of His great love. We did nothing to earn His love, and we can do nothing to lose it. While we can receive His gift confidently, we must also steward it wisely. We don’t obey God to earn His love; we do so in response to the perfect love He has already given us.

John said that “everyone who thus hopes in [Jesus] purifies himself as he is pure” (v. 3). In other words, when you understand that you are already dearly loved by God as His child, you can’t help but respond in gratitude. We are then compelled to purify ourselves just as God is pure, meaning that we seek to become more like Him day after day. The beautiful promise of the gospel is that the more we look to Jesus, the more we will look like Jesus (2 Cor. 3:18). We take part in purifying ourselves by repenting of sin and following His Word; God does the actual work of transforming us. May we keep our eyes focused on God, live as His children, and walk in obedience to become more like Him each day.
content.zh-Hant:
本週稍早，我們研讀了馬太與約翰對耶穌受洗的記載，當時神宣告耶穌是祂的愛子。今天的經文向我們顯明：藉著耶穌，我們也被宣告為神親愛的兒女！我們得以被稱為神的兒女，這事實正是祂偉大慈愛的又一明證。我們沒有做任何事去賺得祂的愛，我們也不能做任何事去失去它。我們固然可以充滿信心地領受祂的禮物，卻也必須明智地作這禮物的管家。我們順服神並不是為了賺得祂的愛；我們順服，乃是回應祂早已賜給我們的完全的愛。

約翰說：「凡向他有這指望的（就是指望耶穌的），就潔淨自己，像他潔淨一樣」（第 3 節）。換句話說，當你明白你身為神的兒女早已被祂深深愛著時，你就不禁要以感恩來回應。於是我們就被激勵去潔淨自己，像神潔淨一樣，意思就是我們尋求日復一日地變得更像祂。福音美麗的應許是：我們越仰望耶穌，就越會像耶穌（林後 3:18）。我們藉著為罪悔改、遵行祂的話語，來參與潔淨自己的過程；而改變我們的真正工作，是神所成就的。願我們定睛仰望神，活出神兒女的樣式，並行在順服中，日日更像祂。

question.en: What does it mean to you that you are a child of God— perfectly loved and sincerely delighted in? Thank God for his great love that you could never earn or lose!
question.zh-Hant: 你是神的兒女——被完全地愛著、被真誠地喜悅著——這對你有甚麼意義？為神那你永遠賺不來、也永遠失不去的偉大慈愛感謝祂吧！

question.en: What is a characteristic of Jesus you need to focus on today in order to become more like him?
question.zh-Hant: 為了變得更像耶穌，今天你需要專注在祂的哪一個特質上？

prayer.en: God, thank you for your wonderful love that I can neither earn nor lose. Help me to live as one who is loved, walking in obedience and trusting you to make me more like you.
prayer.zh-Hant: 神啊，感謝祢那我既賺不來、也失不去的奇妙慈愛。求祢幫助我活得像一個被愛的人，行在順服中，並信靠祢使我更像祢。

content.en:
Acts is the second book written by Luke and is a continuation of his Gospel account—how the work of Jesus persists through the Holy Spirit. When we pick up in Acts 1:8, Jesus has already died on the cross, resurrected, and defeated death forever. These are the final moments before His ascension, when He returned to heaven to reign and rule (Luke 24:50-53). Acts 1:8 is a pivotal verse for all believers, as Jesus gave both a miraculous promise and a missional command. First, the miraculous promise from Jesus is that “you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you.” This is God’s power to equip believers to follow Him and accomplish His plans. In John’s Gospel account, Jesus described the Holy Spirit as the Helper (or Advocate, Comforter) and Spirit of truth, who will be with believers forever (John 14:16-17). When you surrender your life to Jesus by repenting of sin and recognizing Jesus as Lord, you are completely forgiven and made new, and God gifts you with the Holy Spirit, who guides you, empowers you, and forever marks you as His (Eph. 1:13-14).

Next, the missional command from Jesus is to “be my witnesses in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth.” If we look at a map while we read this verse, we see how Jesus commanded the disciples to share the good news in their hometown, surrounding areas, and also the whole world. A witness is someone who tells others what they have experienced firsthand. Those who walk with Jesus and experience His grace, mercy, and compassion should tell their experience to everyone around them. When you have the Holy Spirit through a relationship with Jesus, you also have the power to go wherever God leads, to do whatever He tells you to do, and to be a witness all the days of your life so that others also encounter the miraculous power of God for themselves. Let’s go!
content.zh-Hant:
《使徒行傳》是路加所寫的第二卷書，是他福音記述的延續——講述耶穌的工作如何藉著聖靈持續下去。當我們讀到使徒行傳 1:8 時，耶穌已經在十字架上受死、復活，並永遠擊敗了死亡。這是祂升天前的最後時刻，當祂返回天上作王掌權（路 24:50-53）。使徒行傳 1:8 對所有信徒來說都是一節關鍵的經文，因為耶穌在此賜下了一個神蹟性的應許，也頒下了一個使命性的命令。首先，耶穌所賜神蹟性的應許是「聖靈降臨在你們身上，你們就必得著能力」。這是神的能力，使信徒得以裝備去跟隨祂並成就祂的計劃。在約翰的福音記述中，耶穌形容聖靈為保惠師（或作辯護者、安慰者）和真理的靈，要永遠與信徒同在（約 14:16-17）。當你藉著為罪悔改、承認耶穌為主而將生命交託給耶穌時，你就完全得著赦免、被更新，而神將聖靈賜給你作恩賜；聖靈引導你、賜你能力，並永遠印記你為屬祂的（弗 1:13-14）。

其次，耶穌所頒使命性的命令是要「在耶路撒冷、猶太全地，和撒馬利亞，直到地極，作我的見證」。如果我們一邊讀這節經文一邊看地圖，就會看見耶穌如何命令門徒在他們的家鄉、周圍地區，以及全世界分享這好消息。見證人就是那把自己親身經歷的事告訴別人的人。那些與耶穌同行、經歷過祂的恩典、憐憫與憐恤的人，理當把自己的經歷告訴身邊的每一個人。當你藉著與耶穌的關係擁有聖靈時，你也就有能力去到神所帶領的任何地方、去做祂吩咐你做的任何事，並在你一生的年日裡作見證，好叫別人也能親自遇見神那神蹟性的能力。我們出發吧！

question.en: What is so miraculous about the Holy Spirit giving you power to do everything God leads you to do?
question.zh-Hant: 聖靈賜你能力去做神所帶領你去做的一切事，這有甚麼奇妙之處？

question.en: Where can you live as God’s witness today? Who do you need to have a gospel conversation with today?
question.zh-Hant: 今天你可以在哪裡活出神見證人的樣式？今天你需要與誰進行一次福音的對話？

prayer.en: God, thank you for filling me with your Holy Spirit. Remind me that by your power, grace, and truth, I am able to be a witness for you and accomplish everything you call me to do.
prayer.zh-Hant: 神啊，感謝祢用祢的聖靈充滿我。求祢提醒我：藉著祢的能力、恩典與真理，我能夠為祢作見證，並成就祢呼召我去做的一切事。

content.en:
The life of John the Baptist is a powerful example of boldly proclaiming who God is no matter the cost. Until his last breath, John magnified the name of Jesus and pointed everyone to Him. When you have truly experienced for yourself the miraculous power and compassion of God, you can’t help but share the news. Today’s passage is part of a psalm that shows this same idea. The psalmist encountered God’s righteousness, salvation, and mighty acts over and over again, to the point that he couldn’t count them or fully understand them. When we can’t understand this good news or fully comprehend God’s kindness toward us, we often think, “How can this be?” We can let this question lead us into either unbelieving suspicion or humble submission. Unbelieving suspicion says, “If I can’t fully understand something, it can’t be true,” while humble submission says, “I may not be able to fully understand, but praise God that my faith is so much bigger than what I can grasp and that I am safe in the hands of the One who understands it all.”

Even when we know God is wildly kind to save us, we can grow comfortable, distracted, or numb to the gospel. But if we will fight against the temptation to get “used to” the good news and the miraculous mercy God has shown all of us, we will find ourselves like the psalmist who can’t help but proclaim the goodness of God all the days of his life. Even if you are a follower of Jesus who is afraid to face rejection, unsure of what to say about God to others, or currently numb to God’s goodness, the Holy Spirit will awaken you, fill you, and empower you. If God is as good and worthy as we say that He is (and He is!), let’s make sure every breath we are given tells others about Him!
content.zh-Hant:
施洗約翰的一生，是一個大有能力的榜樣，示範了無論代價如何都要放膽宣揚神是誰。直到嚥下最後一口氣，約翰都在尊崇耶穌的名，並把每個人都指向祂。當你真正親身經歷過神那神蹟性的能力與憐恤時，你就不禁要分享這消息。今天的經文是一篇詩篇的一部分，顯明了同樣的觀念。詩人一次又一次地經歷神的公義、救恩與大能的作為，以致他數算不過來，也無法完全明白。當我們無法明白這好消息，或無法完全領會神向我們所施的恩慈時，我們常常會想：「這怎麼可能呢？」我們可以讓這個問題引領我們走向不信的猜疑，或走向謙卑的順服。不信的猜疑說：「如果我不能完全明白一件事，它就不可能是真的」；而謙卑的順服說：「我或許不能完全明白，但讚美神，我的信心遠遠大過我所能理解的，而我在那位全然明白一切的主手中是安穩的。」

即使我們知道神竟然如此瘋狂地恩慈以致拯救我們，我們仍可能變得安逸、分心，或對福音麻木。但若我們肯抵擋那「習慣」了這好消息、習慣了神向我們眾人所顯神蹟般憐憫的試探，我們就會發現自己像那位詩人一樣，一生的年日都不禁要宣揚神的美善。即或你是一個害怕面對被拒絕、不確定該向別人怎樣談論神、或此刻對神的美善感到麻木的耶穌跟隨者，聖靈也必喚醒你、充滿你、賜你能力。如果神真如我們所說的那樣美善、那樣配得（祂確實是！），就讓我們確保用所領受的每一口氣，都向別人述說祂吧！

question.en: What keeps you from boldly sharing God’s goodness? Write out a prayer confessing these fears.
question.zh-Hant: 是甚麼攔阻你放膽分享神的美善？寫下一個禱告，承認這些恐懼。

question.en: What is one characteristic of God that you have experienced recently?
question.zh-Hant: 你最近所經歷到的神的一個特質是甚麼？

prayer.en: God, while I may not fully understand your goodness and power, I know I can humbly surrender and praise you all my days. Give me the courage to proclaim who you are to a world that desperately needs you.
prayer.zh-Hant: 神啊，我或許不能完全明白祢的美善與能力，但我知道我能謙卑降服，並一生讚美祢。求祢賜我勇氣，向這個極其需要祢的世界宣告祢是誰。
